You are implementing lever (a) in /workspace/SuperGrok1.5 (branch claude/h100-audit-maximal): wire the L3 fused model×optimizer persistent megakernels into the grokking race, with FULL optimizer state (owner directive: no functionality suppressed — a cell that runs with placeholder scalars is suppression).

FILE OWNERSHIP (a sibling agent works concurrently on setup.py/compile.py/build.sh/README — do NOT touch those four): you own csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp, csrc/fused/** (sm_90 cells + megakernel_common/fused_megakernel headers + opt_components.cuh), grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py, grokking_optimizers/megakernel_engine.py, and may add a new validation script under tests/hw/. Do NOT run pip install / setup.py build / any GPU validation — an Optuna tuning run owns the GPU and the live _ops.so right now. Deliver source-complete changes + a runnable validation script + a written build/validate sequence for the operator to run later.

CONTEXT (verified by prior audits — trust these):
- ops.fused_step(model, optimizer, params, input, grad, state, lr) exists in the .so; dispatch.cpp routes it via wired_fused_cell (csrc/fused/fused_wired_cells.inc — all 33 sm_90 cells mapped) → fused_dispatch_table.inc → mega_<model>_<opt>(ctx, params, input, acts, grad, m, v, extra, sizes, offsets, lr, step, stream). All 33 cells are compiled into the .so. dispatch_sm90_cell sets *found=true.
- The race (grokking_race_v2.py) never calls this: grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py _FUSED_REGISTRY={} so has_fused()→False and _try_fused_step always falls back to eager. The only runtime caller of fused_step is megakernel_engine.dispatch_fused_megakernel (used by tests/hw/test_3d_parallel.py).
- CRITICAL GAP (C2): each mega_*.cu host entry binds only pointer state + lr into FusedOptState (see csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh + opt_components.cuh:84-113). Unset fields default: gate=1.0 (SG cosine/sharpness gating inert), d_factor=1.0 (Prodigy d-adaptation inert), bc1/bc2=1.0 (NO Adam bias correction — frozen at t=1), no alpha/lamb/beta1/beta2/eps/wd. The cells are 'compile-verified only' — never executed/numerically validated.

YOUR JOB (source-complete):
1. Extend the fused_step C++ ABI to carry the full scalar set: beta1, beta2, eps, weight_decay, alpha, lamb, gamma, gate, d_factor, bc1, bc2, plus an int64 step. Keep backward compatibility if practical (overload or added-args with defaults); update csrc/bindings/dispatch.cpp fused_step + the m.def binding, the PersistentContext/FusedOptState plumbing, and EVERY sm_90 mega_*.cu host entry (they are generated-style 36-line wrappers — update the generator csrc emission ONLY if that's where they come from (grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py), otherwise update the 33 .cu files consistently; if you regenerate, regenerate ALL cells and the dispatch tables with the same tool so nothing drifts).
2. Per-optimizer scalar binding: each optimizer's step semantics need the right values (e.g. Prodigy needs d_factor from the Python optimizer's state; SG11/15 need their per-step computed gate/alpha; all Adam-family need real bc1/bc2 from per-tensor step counts — note bc is per-PARAM-TENSOR in the per-op path; the megakernel treats the whole flat param as one task today, so a single bc pair per call is acceptable ONLY if step counts are uniform — they are, in the race (all params step together); document this assumption loudly in code.
3. SG meta-net weights: the SG11/SG15 cells' apply (opt_components apply_optimizer<SuperGrok11/15>) reads meta-MLP weights — find how the component consumes them (likely via FusedOptState pointers or constant memory); plumb the real W1/b1/W2/b2/rescale (5 small tensors, fp32) from Python through fused_step (add tensor args or a packed extra-state convention; pick the design that does NOT change per-step ABI cost materially and document it). SuperGrok2's CSA/HCA/PEER/GRU bundle (~30 tensors) is OUT OF SCOPE for this pass: leave its cell on the per-op path via the readiness gate (below) with a loud TODO — that is honest staging, not suppression, because nothing silently degrades.
4. Python wiring: in grokking_optimizers/dispatch.py, implement register_fused population for the validated cells + a READINESS whitelist (explicit set of (model, optimizer) cells allowed to take the megakernel path; everything else uses the existing per-op path and says so ONCE loudly at run start, not per step). In grokking_race_v2.py the _try_fused_step call sites already exist and pass (model_type, opt_name, model, optimizer, x, y, c) — make _try_fused_step actually work for whitelisted cells: it must assemble (params flat view, input, grad, state [m|v|extra] flat, lr, scalars...) from the live optimizer object. NOTE _try_fused_step currently dispatches BEFORE backward (no grads yet!) — the megakernel computes fwd+bwd+opt itself (that's the point); verify the cell consumes raw input+params and produces updated params (read fused_megakernel.cuh to confirm the data flow), and make the race loop skip its own fwd/bwd/eval-grad work when the fused path runs, while keeping eval_every metrics evaluation unchanged.
5. Validation script (tests/hw/test_megakernel_vs_eager.py): for each whitelisted cell, run K=200 steps megakernel vs K=200 steps eager from identical init/data/seed and assert loss-trajectory agreement within a stated tolerance + final param relative error; plus a 3-seed grok smoke for (decoder, adamw). Make it runnable standalone (PYTHONPATH=. python -m tests.hw.test_megakernel_vs_eager --cells decoder:adamw,decoder:lion). DO NOT run it.
6. A BUILD_AND_VALIDATE.md (repo root) with the exact operator sequence: rebuild command, parity gate, your validation script, roofline re-run.

Quality bar: read the actual current ABI/headers before writing; keep the math single-source (apply math stays in csrc/algorithms/*.h — your changes are plumbing, not math); every file you touch must stay compilable in principle (no placeholders); comment WHY at each plumbing site. When done, report: files changed, ABI design chosen, the whitelist you shipped, known risks, and the operator runbook.

1	"""Runtime hardware detection for the fused kernel architecture.
2	
3	Detection is **arch-honest**: ``detect_arch()`` / ``get_gpu_arch()`` report the
4	REAL device architecture, not a collapsed vendor selector. An A100 reports
5	``sm_80``, an L40S ``sm_89``, an H100 ``sm_90a`` — they are NOT all flattened to
6	``90``. AMD reports its real ``gfx<...>`` target; TPU reports ``tpu_v6e``.
7	
8	    NVIDIA: sm_70 / sm_75 / sm_80 / sm_86 / sm_89 / sm_90a / sm_100a / ...
9	    AMD:    gfx906 / gfx908 / gfx90a / gfx942 / gfx950 / gfx110x / ...
10	    TPU:    tpu_v6e
11	
12	The C++ extension is still built as a multi-arch fat binary (one impl per
13	vendor family; see setup.py), so the *fat-binary impl selector* is a separate
14	concern from the reported arch. ``normalize_arch()`` maps a real arch to its
15	impl-family selector (NVIDIA → 90, AMD → 942, TPU → "tpu_v6e") for the code
16	paths that load the matching per-SM/-gfx code from the fat binary. Reporting
17	stays honest; only the binary loader normalises.
18	
19	Feature predicates (``supports_fp8`` etc.) are keyed to the REAL compute
20	capability via ``get_device_sm()``. ``FORCE_ARCH`` accepts any real arch form
21	(``sm_80``, ``gfx942``, ``tpu_v6e``, or a bare numeric CC like ``80``/``90``).
22	"""
23	
24	from __future__ import annotations
25	
26	import functools
27	import logging
28	import os
29	from typing import Union
30	
31	import torch
32	
33	
34	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
35	# Structured logging (spec §6b). A single module logger, env-controlled
36	# level via GROK_LOG_LEVEL (e.g. DEBUG/INFO/WARNING; default WARNING).
37	# Replaces ad-hoc print()s and is the channel for arch-detection / ops-
38	# resolution diagnostics. We attach a NullHandler so importing the package
39	# never configures the root logger (library-friendly); the level is only
40	# applied when the env var is set, so default behaviour is quiet.
41	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
42	logger = logging.getLogger("grokking_optimizers.dispatch")
43	logger.addHandler(logging.NullHandler())
44	
45	
46	def _configure_logging_from_env() -> None:
47	    level_name = os.environ.get("GROK_LOG_LEVEL")
48	    if not level_name:
49	        return
50	    level = getattr(logging, level_name.upper(), None)
51	    if isinstance(level, int):
52	        logger.setLevel(level)
53	        # Only add a stream handler if the user opted in via the env var and
54	        # no real handler exists yet (don't duplicate on re-import).
55	        if not any(not isinstance(h, logging.NullHandler)
56	                   for h in logger.handlers):
57	            handler = logging.StreamHandler()
58	            handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter(
59	                "[%(name)s %(levelname)s] %(message)s"))
60	            logger.addHandler(handler)
61	
62	
63	_configure_logging_from_env()
64	
65	
66	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
67	# Model name normalization — single point of truth for short → canonical.
68	#
69	# Short names ("mamba", "decoder", "vit") are the user-facing API exposed
70	# by profile.MODELS and the CLI. Canonical names ("mamba3",
71	# "transformer_decoder", "vit") are the identifiers used by the
72	# megakernel engine, fused cells, and C++ dispatch. canonicalize_model()
73	# is the ONLY place this mapping is defined.
74	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
75	
76	_MODEL_CANONICAL = {
77	    "mamba": "mamba3",
78	    "decoder": "transformer_decoder",
79	    "vit": "vit",
80	    # Canonical names map to themselves (idempotent).
81	    "mamba3": "mamba3",
82	    "transformer_decoder": "transformer_decoder",
83	}
84	
85	_MODEL_SHORT = {v: k for k, v in {
86	    "mamba": "mamba3",
87	    "decoder": "transformer_decoder",
88	    "vit": "vit",
89	}.items()}
90	
91	
92	def canonicalize_model(name: str) -> str:
93	    """Map a user-facing model name to the canonical internal name.
94	
95	    Short names ("mamba", "decoder", "vit") are the user API (profile.MODELS);
96	    canonical names ("mamba3", "transformer_decoder", "vit") are the megakernel/
97	    fused-cell identifiers. This function accepts either form and returns the
98	    canonical form. Raises ValueError for unknown names.
99	    """
100	    canon = _MODEL_CANONICAL.get(name)
101	    if canon is None:
102	        raise ValueError(
103	            f"Unknown model name {name!r}. "
104	            f"Accepted: {sorted(_MODEL_CANONICAL.keys())}"
105	        )
106	    return canon
107	
108	
109	def short_model_name(canonical: str) -> str:
110	    """Reverse of canonicalize_model: canonical → short user-facing name."""
111	    short = _MODEL_SHORT.get(canonical, canonical)
112	    return short
113	
114	
115	# Every real arch the package recognises (matches the canonical keys in
116	# compile.ARCH_TABLE). Reporting is honest against this set; the fat-binary
117	# impl selector (90/942) is a separate, normalised value (see normalize_arch).
118	SUPPORTED_ARCHES = (
119	    # NVIDIA — real compute capabilities (the ``a`` suffix is the canonical
120	    # spelling for the arch-conditional variants, matching compile.ARCH_TABLE).
121	    "sm_70", "sm_75", "sm_80", "sm_86", "sm_89",
122	    "sm_90a", "sm_100a", "sm_103a", "sm_120a",
123	    # AMD — real gfx targets.
124	    "gfx906", "gfx908", "gfx90a", "gfx942", "gfx950",
125	    "gfx1030", "gfx1100", "gfx1101", "gfx1102",
126	    "gfx1151", "gfx1200", "gfx1201",
127	    # TPU.
128	    "tpu_v6e",
129	)
130	
131	# The two GPU fat-binary impl families the extension actually ships. Real
132	# arches normalise onto one of these (plus "tpu_v6e") via normalize_arch().
133	IMPL_FAMILIES = (90, 942, "tpu_v6e")
134	
135	
136	class UnsupportedArchError(RuntimeError):
137	    """Raised when the detected arch is not one of {sm_90, gfx942, tpu_v6e}."""
138	
139	
140	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
141	# Vendor / backend
142	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
143	
144	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
145	def get_gpu_vendor() -> str:
146	    """GPU vendor: 'nvidia', 'amd', or 'none' (no GPU)."""
147	    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
148	        return 'none'
149	    if hasattr(torch.version, 'hip') and torch.version.hip is not None:
150	        return 'amd'
151	    return 'nvidia'
152	
153	
154	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
155	def get_backend() -> str:
156	    """Active backend: 'cuda', 'hip', or 'cpu'."""
157	    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
158	        return 'cpu'
159	    if hasattr(torch.version, 'hip') and torch.version.hip is not None:
160	        return 'hip'
161	    return 'cuda'
162	
163	
164	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
165	def get_warp_size() -> int:
166	    """Warp/wavefront size: 32 (NVIDIA), 64 (AMD CDNA)."""
167	    if get_gpu_vendor() == 'amd':
168	        return 64
169	    return 32
170	
171	
172	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
173	# Arch detection
174	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
175	
176	# Real NVIDIA compute capabilities the package recognises, in ascending
177	# order, mapped to their canonical arch-label spelling. A device CC is
178	# resolved to the highest label it is >= to (so a future sm_91 still resolves
179	# to the sm_90a kernel family, never silently dropping to fp32).
180	_NVIDIA_CC_LABELS = (
181	    (70, "sm_70"), (75, "sm_75"), (80, "sm_80"), (86, "sm_86"),
182	    (89, "sm_89"), (90, "sm_90a"), (100, "sm_100a"), (103, "sm_103a"),
183	    (120, "sm_120a"),
184	)
185	
186	
187	def _sm_to_arch_label(cc: int) -> str:
188	    """Map a real NVIDIA compute capability int to its canonical arch label.
189	
190	    Honest: an A100 (CC 80) → ``sm_80``, an L40S (CC 89) → ``sm_89``, an H100
191	    (CC 90) → ``sm_90a``. A CC above the highest known entry resolves to that
192	    highest label (forward-compatible), a CC below the lowest raises.
193	    """
194	    label = None
195	    for threshold, name in _NVIDIA_CC_LABELS:
196	        if cc >= threshold:
197	            label = name
198	    if label is None:
199	        raise UnsupportedArchError(
200	            f"NVIDIA compute capability {cc} is below the minimum supported "
201	            f"(sm_70).")
202	    return label
203	
204	
205	def _normalize_force_arch(force: str) -> Union[int, str]:
206	    """Map a FORCE_ARCH string to the REAL arch it names (honest).
207	
208	    Returns a real arch label (``sm_80``/``gfx942``/...) or ``tpu_v6e``. A bare
209	    numeric value is treated as an NVIDIA compute capability and resolved to its
210	    real label. Raises on unrecognised input. Use :func:`normalize_arch` on the
211	    result when an impl-family selector (90/942) is needed.
212	    """
213	    if force.startswith('tpu'):
214	        return "tpu_v6e"
215	    # AMD: any gfx target. Honor the exact gfx label; the bare ``942`` form maps
216	    # to gfx942 for back-compat.
217	    if force.startswith('gfx'):
218	        return force
219	    if force == '942':
220	        return "gfx942"
221	    # NVIDIA: sm_* label (normalise the bare ``sm_90`` alias to ``sm_90a`` etc.)
222	    if force.startswith('sm_'):
223	        try:
224	            cc = int(force[3:].rstrip('a'))
225	        except ValueError:
226	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
227	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
228	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
229	    if force.startswith('sm'):
230	        try:
231	            cc = int(force[2:].rstrip('a'))
232	        except ValueError:
233	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
234	                f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized.") from None
235	        return _sm_to_arch_label(cc)
236	    # Bare numeric compute capability (e.g. ``80`` for A100, ``90`` for H100).
237	    if force.isdigit():
238	        return _sm_to_arch_label(int(force))
239	    raise UnsupportedArchError(
240	        f"FORCE_ARCH={force!r} not recognized. Use an NVIDIA arch "
241	        f"(sm_70..sm_120a or a numeric CC), an AMD arch (gfx906..gfx1201), "
242	        f"or tpu_v6e.")
243	
244	
245	def normalize_arch(arch: Union[int, str]) -> Union[int, str]:
246	    """Map a real arch to its fat-binary impl-family selector.
247	
248	    NVIDIA labels (``sm_*``) and bare CC ints → ``90``; AMD ``gfx*`` (and the
249	    bare ``942``) → ``942``; ``tpu_v6e`` → ``"tpu_v6e"``. This is the ONLY place
250	    the NVIDIA→90 / AMD→942 collapse happens, and it is used solely by the code
251	    that loads the matching per-arch code from the multi-arch fat binary — never
252	    for *reporting* the device's real arch.
253	    """
254	    if arch == "tpu_v6e":
255	        return "tpu_v6e"
256	    if isinstance(arch, int):
257	        return 942 if arch == 942 else 90
258	    if arch.startswith('gfx'):
259	        return 942
260	    if arch.startswith('sm'):
261	        return 90
262	    raise UnsupportedArchError(f"Cannot normalize unknown arch {arch!r}")
263	
264	
265	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
266	def get_gpu_arch() -> Union[int, str]:
267	    """Detected REAL GPU arch label: ``sm_80`` / ``sm_90a`` / ``gfx942`` / ...
268	
269	    Reports the device's actual compute capability (NVIDIA) or gfx target (AMD)
270	    — NOT a collapsed vendor selector. Use :func:`normalize_arch` on the result
271	    when the fat-binary impl-family int (90/942) is needed.
272	
273	    Honors FORCE_ARCH. Raises ``UnsupportedArchError`` if no GPU is available
274	    or the vendor is unknown.
275	    """
276	    force = os.environ.get('FORCE_ARCH')
277	    if force:
278	        sel = _normalize_force_arch(force)
279	        if sel == "tpu_v6e":
280	            raise UnsupportedArchError(
281	                "FORCE_ARCH=tpu_v6e is not a GPU arch; use detect_arch() instead")
282	        return sel
283	
284	    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
285	        raise UnsupportedArchError(
286	            "No CUDA/HIP device available. Set FORCE_ARCH (e.g. sm_80 for an "
287	            "A100, sm_90a for an H100, gfx942 for MI300X) for cross-arch "
288	            "testing.")
289	
290	    vendor = get_gpu_vendor()
291	    if vendor == 'nvidia':
292	        return _sm_to_arch_label(get_device_sm())  # real CC -> real label
293	    if vendor == 'amd':
294	        return _amd_gfx_label()                     # real gfx target
295	    raise UnsupportedArchError(f"Unknown GPU vendor {vendor!r}")
296	
297	
298	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
299	def _amd_gfx_label() -> str:
300	    """Real AMD gfx target string (e.g. ``gfx942``), or ``gfx942`` if unknown.
301	
302	    Reads the device's gcnArchName via torch and strips any ``:xnack`` feature
303	    suffix. Falls back to ``gfx942`` (the shipped CDNA3 impl) only when the
304	    runtime exposes no arch name.
305	    """
306	    try:
307	        props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.cuda.current_device())
308	        name = getattr(props, "gcnArchName", None) or ""
309	    except Exception:
310	        name = ""
311	    name = name.split(":", 1)[0].strip()
312	    if name.startswith("gfx"):
313	        return name
314	    return "gfx942"
315	
316	
317	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
318	def get_device_sm():
319	    """Real NVIDIA compute capability (e.g. 70, 80, 90, 120), or None.
320	
321	    None when there is no NVIDIA device (CPU host or AMD). Used by the feature
322	    predicates that want the raw integer CC; ``get_gpu_arch()`` returns the
323	    same capability as a canonical arch *label*.
324	    """
325	    if get_gpu_vendor() != 'nvidia':
326	        return None
327	    major, minor = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
328	    return major * 10 + minor
329	
330	
331	@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1)
332	def detect_arch() -> Union[int, str]:
333	    """Detect the active REAL arch: a label like ``sm_80`` / ``sm_90a`` /
334	    ``gfx942``, or ``"tpu_v6e"``.
335	
336	    Detection order:
337	      1. FORCE_ARCH env var (accepts sm_*, gfx*, a numeric CC, or tpu_v6e)
338	      2. TPU detection via JAX
339	      3. GPU detection via get_gpu_arch()
340

450	# C++ extension loader (consolidated from _ops_loader.py).
451	# Loads the per-arch specialized C++ extension. Raises on first kernel
452	# attribute access if the extension isn't built — there is no Python
453	# fallback path, but `import grokking_optimizers` succeeds either way so
454	# that profiling / tooling code can introspect the package without a

459	class _LazyOps:
460	    """Lazy proxy for the compiled `grokking_optimizers._ops` extension.
461	
462	    Resolves on first attribute access. `hasattr(_ops, "foo")` correctly
463	    returns False when the extension isn't built; direct attribute access
464	    raises AttributeError with a descriptive build hint. This preserves the
465	    no-fallback contract (kernels are unreachable without a build) while
466	    allowing import-time introspection.
467	    """
468	    __slots__ = ("_real", "_error", "_attr_cache")
469	
470	    def __init__(self):
471	        object.__setattr__(self, "_real", None)
472	        object.__setattr__(self, "_error", None)
473	        # Memoize resolved kernel attributes so repeated `_ops.fn` access on
474	        # the hot path skips the module getattr after the first lookup.
475	        object.__setattr__(self, "_attr_cache", {})
476	
477	    def _resolve(self):
478	        if self._real is not None:
479	            return self._real
480	        if self._error is not None:
481	            return None  # cached failure
482	        try:
483	            import importlib
484	            real = importlib.import_module("grokking_optimizers._ops")
485	            object.__setattr__(self, "_real", real)
486	            return real
487	        except ImportError as e:
488	            object.__setattr__(self, "_error", e)
489	            logger.debug("grokking_optimizers._ops not importable "
490	                         "(extension unbuilt?): %s", e)
491	            return None
492	
493	    def __getattr__(self, name):
494	        if name.startswith("_"):
495	            raise AttributeError(name)
496	        cache = self._attr_cache
497	        cached = cache.get(name)
498	        if cached is not None:
499	            return cached
500	        real = self._resolve()
501	        if real is None:
502	            raise AttributeError(
503	                f"grokking_optimizers._ops.{name}: C++ extension not built. "
504	                f"Run `pip install -e .` (supported arches: {SUPPORTED_ARCHES}). "
505	                f"Original ImportError: {self._error}"
506	            )
507	        attr = getattr(real, name)
508	        cache[name] = attr
509	        return attr
510	
511	    def bind(self, name):
512	        """Resolve ``name`` once and return the underlying kernel callable.
513	
514	        Callers (optimizers) cache the returned bound function on the instance
515	        so subsequent steps skip the proxy ``__getattr__`` entirely. Raises the
516	        same descriptive error as attribute access if the extension is unbuilt.
517	        """
518	        return self.__getattr__(name)
519	
520	    def __bool__(self):
521	        return self._resolve() is not None
522	
523	    def __repr__(self):
524	        real = self._resolve()
525	        if real is None:
526	            return f"<_LazyOps unbuilt: {self._error}>"
527	        return f"<_LazyOps wrapping {real!r}>"
528	
529	
530	_cached_ops = _LazyOps()
531	
532	
533	def get_ops():
534	    """Return the lazy `_ops` proxy. Never raises at call time."""
535	    return _cached_ops

549	def has_kernels() -> bool:
550	    """True iff the compiled C++/CUDA/HIP kernel extension is importable AND
551	    exposes the fused optimizer kernels.
552	
553	    This is the honest capability flag (spec §6a): the optimizers have NO
554	    pure-PyTorch fallback for ``.step()`` — they hard-require this extension and

1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel_engine — §8.4 fused-kernel ↔ framework adapter.
2	
3	THE TRICKY PART (§8.4). DeepSpeed and Megatron-LM are both built around a
4	**separate** forward / backward / `optimizer.step()` interface:
5	
6	    out  = engine(batch)        # forward
7	    engine.backward(loss)       # backward — populates .grad on every param
8	    engine.step()               # optimizer.step() + grad clear
9	
10	But the Stage-6 megakernel (``grokking_optimizers.megakernel``) is a **fused L3
11	single launch**: one persistent kernel does forward **and** backward **and** the
12	optimizer update inside one kernel invocation (``FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT``).
13	There is no separate backward to hook, and no separate `.step()` — the fused
14	launch already did all three. The framework's contract and the fused kernel's
15	contract are therefore in direct conflict.
16	
17	This module is the **adapter** that reconciles them. It does two things:
18	
19	1. :class:`MegakernelOptimizer` — a ``torch.optim.Optimizer`` subclass that
20	   presents the fused step as a standard ``.step()`` so DeepSpeed/Megatron can
21	   drive it as a ``client_optimizer``. Its ``.step()`` is where the actual fused
22	   launch is invoked (for L3) or where the inner optimizer's real ``.step()``
23	   runs (for L1/L2). It degrades to a plain pass-through optimizer when no
24	   framework is present.
25	
26	2. :class:`FusedBackwardHook` — intercepts / no-ops the framework's separate
27	   ``.backward()`` **when the fused path owns fwd+bwd+opt** (L3). When the fused
28	   kernel already produced gradients-and-update in the forward launch, letting
29	   the framework run its own autograd backward would (a) waste a full backward
30	   pass and (b) double-apply the update. The hook short-circuits the framework
31	   backward and instead just marks gradients as "owned by the fused kernel" so
32	   ``.step()`` knows not to re-run them.
33	
34	The decision of *which* mode a given (model, optimizer, arch) cell is in comes
35	from the Stage-6 solver: :func:`grokking_optimizers.megakernel.solve` returns a
36	:class:`~grokking_optimizers.megakernel.FusionPlan` whose ``tier`` tells us how
37	much the fused kernel owns. The control flow below is keyed entirely off that
38	tier.
39	
40	────────────────────────────── CONTROL FLOW ──────────────────────────────────
41	
42	  query solve(model, optimizer, arch) → plan.tier
43	
44	  ┌─ L3_FWD_BWD_OPT  (fused kernel owns fwd + bwd + opt) ─────────────────────┐
45	  │  forward(batch):                                                          │
46	  │     • the fused L3 launch runs fwd+bwd+opt in ONE kernel.                 │
47	  │     • returns loss; gradients + the parameter update are ALREADY applied. │
48	  │     • adapter sets `_fused_owned = True`.                                 │
49	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
50	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → True → **NO-OP**. The framework's  │
51	  │       autograd backward is suppressed (it would redo work + double-apply).│
52	  │  engine.step()  →  MegakernelOptimizer.step():                           │
53	  │     • sees `_fused_owned` → the update already happened in forward → it   │
54	  │       only does framework bookkeeping (zero_grad bookkeeping, lr-sched    │
55	  │       coupling) and returns. It does NOT re-run the optimizer math.       │
56	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
57	
58	  ┌─ L2_BWD_OPT  (fused kernel owns bwd + opt; framework owns fwd) ───────────┐
59	  │  forward(batch):  framework's normal forward (autograd graph built).      │
60	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
61	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → True for the FUSED region: the     │
62	  │       fused bwd+opt launch runs, producing grads + applying the update.   │
63	  │     • framework autograd backward is suppressed for the fused params.     │
64	  │  engine.step():  update already applied by the fused bwd+opt → no-op math.│
65	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
66	
67	  ┌─ L1_OPT_ONLY  (fused kernel owns ONLY the optimizer step) ────────────────┐
68	  │  forward(batch):  framework forward.                                      │
69	  │  engine.backward(loss):                                                   │
70	  │     • FusedBackwardHook.intercepts() → False → framework runs its OWN     │
71	  │       autograd backward normally (grads populated the usual way).         │
72	  │  engine.step()  →  MegakernelOptimizer.step():                           │
73	  │     • runs the fused optimizer-only kernel via the wrapped optimizer's    │
74	  │       real `.step()` (which itself dispatches to the L1 fused tail).      │
75	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
76	
77	  ┌─ L0_UNFUSED  (no fusion — solver would have errored for a megakernel) ────┐
78	  │  Pure pass-through: framework fwd, framework bwd, wrapped optimizer step. │
79	  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
80	
81	IMPORT SAFETY. This module imports only ``torch`` and the pure-Python Stage-6
82	solver at module load. The DeepSpeed / Megatron framework objects are *never*
83	imported here; the adapter is shaped to fit their duck-typed `client_optimizer`
84	/ backward-hook protocols, so it works when they are present and degrades to a
85	plain torch optimizer when they are absent. No GPU, no launched job, and no
86	DeepSpeed are required to import or unit-test the dispatch logic.
87	"""

101	def dispatch_fused_megakernel(model: str, optimizer: str, *, params=None,
102	                              grads=None, opt_state=None, inputs=None,
103	                              lr: float = 1e-3, state=None):
104	    """Route a fused L3/L1 megakernel step to the backend for the detected arch.
105	
106	    The single cross-arch entry that unifies the three real composition paths
107	    (Phase 3):
108	      * tpu_v6e → csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused.fused_step (jax.jit fused
109	        program; the 33 tpu cells bind to it).
110	      * sm_90 / gfx942 → the C++ `fused_step` pybind (dispatch.cpp routes to the
111	        real composed `mega_<model>_<opt>` launcher; gfx942 host launch is 🟡).
112	
113	    Returns the backend's result (TPU: (new_params, new_state)). Raises a clear
114	    error if the cell/binding is unavailable on this build (no silent no-op).
115	    """
116	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import detect_arch, normalize_arch
117	    arch = detect_arch()
118	    # detect_arch() now reports the REAL arch (e.g. sm_80 / sm_90a / gfx942).
119	    # The megakernel solver keys on the impl-family label ("sm_90"/"gfx942"/
120	    # "tpu_v6e"), so normalise the real arch to its family for the solve() call.
121	    impl = normalize_arch(arch)
122	    solver_arch = (impl if isinstance(impl, str)
123	                   else ("sm_90" if impl == 90 else "gfx942"))
124	    tier = ("L3" if solve(model, optimizer, solver_arch).tier
125	            == FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT else "L1")
126	    if arch == "tpu_v6e":
127	        from csrc.backends.pallas._pallas_fused import fused_step as tpu_fused
128	        return tpu_fused(model, optimizer, params=params, grads=grads,
129	                         opt_state=opt_state, inputs=inputs, lr=lr, tier=tier)
130	    # NVIDIA / AMD: the C++ megakernel dispatch (real composition per dispatch.cpp).
131	    from grokking_optimizers.dispatch import get_ops
132	    ops = get_ops()
133	    if not hasattr(ops, "fused_step"):
134	        raise RuntimeError(
135	            "C++ fused_step binding unavailable; build the extension "
136	            "(WITH_CUDA/WITH_HIP) to use the GPU fused megakernel path.")
137	    if params is None or state is None:
138	        raise ValueError("GPU fused_step needs params, grads, and a state tensor "
139	                         "([m|v|extra] per param-tensor).")
140	    ops.fused_step(model, optimizer, params,
141	                   inputs if inputs is not None else params,
142	                   grads if grads is not None else params, state, float(lr))
143	    return params

189	class FusedBackwardHook:
190	    """Intercepts / no-ops the framework's separate backward when fused (§8.4).
191	
192	    Usage shapes (both duck-typed, framework-agnostic):
193	
194	    * **Explicit guard** — wrap the framework backward call::
195	
196	          if not hook.intercept_backward(loss):
197	              engine.backward(loss)   # framework path (L0/L1 only)
198	
199	      ``intercept_backward`` returns True when the fused kernel already owns the
200	      backward (L2/L3), in which case the framework backward is skipped and the
201	      fused launch is invoked instead.
202	
203	    * **Tensor hook** — :meth:`as_tensor_hook` returns a callable suitable for
204	      ``loss.register_hook(...)`` that zeroes the incoming grad when the fused
205	      path owns it, so an accidental ``loss.backward()`` is neutralized rather
206	      than double-applying.
207	    """
208	
209	    def __init__(
210	        self,
211	        plan: Optional[FusionPlan],
212	        fused_launch: Optional[Callable[..., Any]] = None,
213	    ) -> None:
214	        self.plan = plan
215	        # The callable that actually performs the fused bwd(+opt) launch. In the
216	        # real build this routes into the dispatch.cpp fused TU; here it is
217	        # injected so the control flow is testable without a kernel.
218	        self._fused_launch = fused_launch
219	        # Set True after a fused launch has applied the update this iteration,
220	        # so MegakernelOptimizer.step() knows the math already ran.
221	        self.fused_update_applied = False
222	
223	    @property
224	    def owns_backward(self) -> bool:
225	        return fused_owns_backward(self.plan)
226	
227	    def intercept_backward(self, loss: "torch.Tensor", **kwargs: Any) -> bool:
228	        """Decide whether to suppress the framework backward.
229	
230	        Returns
231	        -------
232	        bool
233	            True  → the fused kernel owns backward (L2/L3); the framework's
234	                    ``.backward()`` was suppressed and the fused launch (if
235	                    provided) was invoked here instead.
236	            False → L0/L1; the caller must run the framework backward itself.
237	        """
238	        if not self.owns_backward:
239	            return False
240	        # Fused path owns backward: run the fused launch (bwd[+opt]) if wired,
241	        # and mark the update as applied so .step() is a no-op on the math.
242	        if self._fused_launch is not None:
243	            self._fused_launch(loss, **kwargs)
244	        self.fused_update_applied = fused_owns_step(self.plan)
245	        return True
246	
247	    def as_tensor_hook(self) -> Callable[["torch.Tensor"], "torch.Tensor"]:
248	        """Return a ``Tensor.register_hook`` callable that neutralizes grads.
249	
250	        If the fused path owns backward and an autograd backward is nonetheless
251	        triggered, this zeroes the gradient flowing back so nothing is
252	        double-counted. A pass-through (identity) when the framework legitimately
253	        owns backward (L0/L1).
254	        """
255	
256	        owns = self.owns_backward
257	
258	        def _hook(grad: "torch.Tensor") -> "torch.Tensor":
259	            if owns:
260	                return torch.zeros_like(grad)
261	            return grad
262	
263	        return _hook
264	
265	    def reset(self) -> None:
266	        """Clear per-iteration state (call at the top of each training step)."""
267	        self.fused_update_applied = False
268	
269	
270	# ─────────────────────────── MegakernelOptimizer ─────────────────────────────
271	
272	
273	class MegakernelOptimizer(Optimizer):
274	    """Present the fused L3 megakernel step as a standard ``torch.optim`` step.
275	
276	    Wraps an *inner* optimizer (one of the 11 race optimizers — an
277	    ``Optimizer`` whose real ``.step()`` dispatches into the fused kernel for the
278	    L1 optimizer-only tail). Depending on the fusion tier reported by the
279	    Stage-6 solver, ``.step()`` either:
280	
281	    * **L3 / L2** — the fused launch (driven through :class:`FusedBackwardHook`
282	      during the forward/backward phase) already applied the parameter update;
283	      ``.step()`` performs only framework bookkeeping and returns. It does NOT
284	      re-run the optimizer math (that would double-apply).
285	    * **L1 / L0** — calls the inner optimizer's real ``.step()`` (which itself
286	      fuses the optimizer-only tail at L1, or runs unfused at L0).
287	
288	    The class satisfies DeepSpeed's ``client_optimizer`` shape: it subclasses
289	    ``torch.optim.Optimizer``, exposes ``param_groups`` / ``state`` (delegated to
290	    the inner optimizer), and a no-arg-compatible ``.step()``. With no framework
291	    present it behaves as a transparent wrapper around the inner optimizer.
292	    """
293	
294	    def __init__(
295	        self,
296	        inner_optimizer: Optimizer,
297	        model_name: str,
298	        arch: str,
299	        optimizer_name: Optional[str] = None,
300	        hook: Optional[FusedBackwardHook] = None,
301	    ) -> None:
302	        if not isinstance(inner_optimizer, Optimizer):
303	            raise TypeError(
304	                "inner_optimizer must be a torch.optim.Optimizer, got "
305	                f"{type(inner_optimizer).__name__}"
306	            )
307	        self.inner = inner_optimizer
308	        self.model_name = model_name
309	        self.arch = arch
310	        self.optimizer_name = optimizer_name or _infer_optimizer_name(inner_optimizer)
311	        self.plan = resolve_fusion_plan(self.model_name, self.optimizer_name, self.arch)
312	        self.hook = hook or FusedBackwardHook(self.plan)
313	        # We deliberately do NOT call super().__init__ with fresh defaults — we
314	        # delegate param_groups/state to the inner optimizer so DeepSpeed sees
315	        # the real parameters, learning rates, and state. The Optimizer
316	        # protocol only requires param_groups + state + step + zero_grad, all of
317	        # which we forward.
318	        self.defaults = getattr(inner_optimizer, "defaults", {})
319	
320	    # ── Optimizer protocol delegation (DeepSpeed client_optimizer shape) ─────
321	
322	    @property
323	    def param_groups(self):  # type: ignore[override]
324	        return self.inner.param_groups
325	
326	    @param_groups.setter
327	    def param_groups(self, value):  # type: ignore[override]
328	        self.inner.param_groups = value
329	
330	    @property
331	    def state(self):  # type: ignore[override]
332	        return self.inner.state
333	
334	    @state.setter
335	    def state(self, value):  # type: ignore[override]
336	        self.inner.state = value
337	
338	    def state_dict(self):
339	        return self.inner.state_dict()
340	
341	    def load_state_dict(self, state_dict):
342	        return self.inner.load_state_dict(state_dict)
343	
344	    def zero_grad(self, set_to_none: bool = True):  # type: ignore[override]
345	        return self.inner.zero_grad(set_to_none=set_to_none)
346	
347	    def add_param_group(self, param_group):
348	        return self.inner.add_param_group(param_group)
349	
350	    # ── the fused-aware step (the §8.4 reconciliation point) ─────────────────
351	
352	    @torch.no_grad()
353	    def step(self, closure: Optional[Callable[[], float]] = None):  # type: ignore[override]
354	        """Fused-aware optimizer step.
355	
356	        Control flow (mirrors the module docstring):
357	
358	        * If the fused kernel already applied the update this iteration
359	          (``hook.fused_update_applied`` — set by :class:`FusedBackwardHook` for
360	          L2/L3), the math is **already done**: we only run the closure (for
361	          loss reporting) and reset the hook, then return. Re-running
362	          ``inner.step()`` here would double-apply the update.
363	        * Otherwise (L0/L1, or no fused launch happened), delegate to the inner
364	          optimizer's real ``.step()`` — which fuses the optimizer-only tail at
365	          L1 or runs unfused at L0.
366	        """
367	        loss = None
368	        if closure is not None:
369	            with torch.enable_grad():
370	                loss = closure()
371	
372	        if fused_owns_step(self.plan) and self.hook.fused_update_applied:
373	            # L2/L3 fused path already updated the params in the fused launch.
374	            # Bookkeeping only — do NOT re-run the optimizer math.
375	            self.hook.reset()
376	            return loss
377	
378	        # L0/L1 (or fused launch did not run this step): real optimizer step.
379	        result = self.inner.step()
380	        self.hook.reset()
381	        return loss if loss is not None else result
382	
383	    # ── convenience for the framework-driven training loop ───────────────────
384	
385	    def backward(self, loss: "torch.Tensor", **kwargs: Any) -> bool:
386	        """Framework-facing backward shim.
387	
388	        Returns True if the fused kernel owned (and performed) the backward, in
389	        which case the caller must NOT also run the framework autograd backward.
390	        Returns False for L0/L1, signalling the caller to run its own backward.
391	        """
392	        return self.hook.intercept_backward(loss, **kwargs)
393	
394	    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - cosmetic
395	        tier = _tier_of(self.plan).name
396	        return (
397	            f"MegakernelOptimizer(inner={type(self.inner).__name__}, "
398	            f"model={self.model_name!r}, arch={self.arch!r}, "
399	            f"optimizer={self.optimizer_name!r}, tier={tier})"
400	        )
401	
402	
403	def _infer_optimizer_name(opt: Optimizer) -> str:
404	    """Best-effort map from an optimizer instance to its solver name key.
405	
406	    The Stage-6 solver keys on the lower-cased canonical names in
407	    ``megakernel.OPTIMIZERS``. We match by class name, tolerating the common
408	    ``SuperGrok2`` → ``supergrok2`` spelling. Unknown ⇒ returns the lowercased
409	    class name (the solver will report it as unknown and the adapter falls back
410	    to the unfused path).
411	    """
412	    from grokking_optimizers.megakernel import OPTIMIZERS  # lazy, pure-Python
413	
414	    cls = type(opt).__name__.lower()
415	    # Strip common decorator prefixes.
416	    for prefix in ("compiled", "moeaware"):
417	        if cls.startswith(prefix):
418	            cls = cls[len(prefix):]
419	    if cls in OPTIMIZERS:
420	        return cls
421	    # Map e.g. "grokadamw" already matches; "looksam" matches; fall through.
422	    for canon in OPTIMIZERS:
423	        if cls == canon:
424	            return canon
425	    return cls
426	
427	
428	def build_client_optimizer(
429	    inner_optimizer: Optimizer,
430	    model_name: str,
431	    arch: str,
432	    optimizer_name: Optional[str] = None,
433	) -> MegakernelOptimizer:
434	    """Factory: wrap ``inner_optimizer`` as a fused-aware DeepSpeed client_optimizer.
435	
436	    Hand the returned object to ``deepspeed.initialize(optimizer=...)`` (or use
437	    it directly in a plain torch loop). It carries its own
438	    :class:`FusedBackwardHook`, reachable as ``.hook`` for the backward-shim
439	    wiring in the training loop.
440	    """
441	    return MegakernelOptimizer(
442	        inner_optimizer=inner_optimizer,
443	        model_name=model_name,
444	        arch=arch,
445	        optimizer_name=optimizer_name,
446	    )
447	
448	
449	def fused_training_step(
450	    optimizer: MegakernelOptimizer,
451	    loss: "torch.Tensor",
452	    framework_backward: Optional[Callable[["torch.Tensor"], None]] = None,
453	) -> None:
454	    """Reference glue for one fused-aware training step (§8.4 control flow).
455	
456	    Encapsulates the backward/step reconciliation so a framework loop (or the
457	    test harness) can call a single function:
458	
459	        1. Ask the hook whether the fused kernel owns backward.
460	        2. If not (L0/L1), run ``framework_backward(loss)`` (the engine's
461	           autograd backward).
462	        3. Call ``optimizer.step()`` — which is a no-op on the math for L2/L3
463	           (already applied) and the real step for L0/L1.
464	
465	    ``framework_backward`` defaults to ``loss.backward`` when not supplied.
466	    """
467	    if not optimizer.backward(loss):
468	        bwd = framework_backward or (lambda x: x.backward())
469	        bwd(loss)
470	    optimizer.step()
471	
472	
473	def all_reduce_optimizer_hooks(
474	    optimizer: Optimizer, params: Optional[Iterable["torch.Tensor"]] = None
475	) -> None:
476	    """Invoke an optimizer's existing data-parallel allreduce hooks if present.
477	
478	    Several race optimizers (notably SuperGrok2 via ``_allreduce_meta_grads`` /
479	    ``_allreduce_expert_counts``) already carry DP-aware allreduce hooks. The
480	    distributed layer calls this before the fused step so those hooks fire under
481	    the launched job; it is a guarded no-op when the hooks/job are absent.
482	    """
483	    inner = getattr(optimizer, "inner", optimizer)
484	    for hook_name in ("_allreduce_meta_grads", "_allreduce_expert_counts"):
485	        fn = getattr(inner, hook_name, None)
486	        if callable(fn):
487	            try:
488	                fn()
489	            except Exception:
490	                # Hooks self-guard on dist.is_initialized(); never fatal here.
491	                pass
492	    _ = params
493	
494	
495	__all__ = [
496	    "MegakernelOptimizer",
497	    "FusedBackwardHook",
498	    "resolve_fusion_plan",
499	    "fused_owns_backward",
500	    "fused_owns_step",
501	    "build_client_optimizer",
502	    "fused_training_step",
503	    "all_reduce_optimizer_hooks",
504	    "dispatch_fused_megakernel",
505	]

1	#ifndef SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
2	#define SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_
3	// ============================================================================
4	// csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh — REAL per-optimizer device-function
5	// composition library for the sm_90 fused L3 megakernel (Phase 3 Stage 5).
6	//
7	// THIS REPLACES THE FALSE POSITIVE. The previous fused path (megakernel_demo.cu
8	// :opt_update<Opt>) implemented only 4 optimizers (AdamW/Lion/Muon/SuperGrok15)
9	// with TOY math, and the codegen mapped the other 7 to the AdamW tail — i.e.
10	// `mega_*_prodigy.cu` actually ran AdamW. That is the breadth-faking this stage
11	// eliminates.
12	//
13	// Here every one of the 11 optimizers calls its OWN, REAL per-element update
14	// function from csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h (the canonical optimizer component —
15	// the same device functions the per-op launchers compile). No fallback, no
16	// templating one optimizer from another, no toy substitute. Each optimizer's
17	// genuine state buffers are plumbed through FusedOptState.
18	//
19	// SCOPE / HONESTY (the fused TAIL vs the outer loop):
20	//   The L3 megakernel fuses the per-element optimizer TAIL after fwd+bwd. The
21	//   multi-phase OUTER parts that are not per-element — Muon's Newton–Schulz
22	//   orthogonalization, Prodigy's global d reduction, LookSAM's perturb/restore
23	//   ascent, SG11/SG15's cosine-gate reduction, and SG2's CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net
24	//   — run as their own launch(es) and hand this tail the precomputed result
25	//   (orth direction, d factor, sam_dir, reduced gate, smart-grad). This mirrors
26	//   the real per-op pipelines exactly; the tail math below IS the real apply.
27	// ============================================================================
28	
29	#include <cuda_runtime.h>
30	#include <cstdint>
31	
32	// The 11 canonical optimizer components (real per-element device functions).
33	#include "csrc/algorithms/adamw.h"
34	#include "csrc/algorithms/lion.h"
35	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokfast.h"
36	#include "csrc/algorithms/grokadamw.h"
37	#include "csrc/algorithms/looksam.h"
38	#include "csrc/algorithms/prodigy.h"
39	#include "csrc/algorithms/neuralgrok.h"
40	#include "csrc/algorithms/muon.h"
41	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h"
42	#include "csrc/algorithms/supergrok15.h"
43	// SG2's elementwise tail is an Adam apply on the meta-net smart-grad; the
44	// metanet itself (supergrok2.h / supergrok2_bilevel_adjoint.h) is the separate
45	// CSA/HCA launch. adamw.h already pulled in above covers the tail.
46	
47	namespace sg { namespace fused { namespace sm90 {
48	
49	namespace algo = ::sg::algorithms;
50	
51	// Compile-time optimizer selector — one value per real optimizer (no aliases,
52	// no fallback). Must match grokking_optimizers/megakernel_codegen.py's set.
53	enum class OptId : int {
54	    AdamW = 0, Lion = 1, Grokfast = 2, GrokAdamW = 3, LookSAM = 4,
55	    Prodigy = 5, NeuralGrok = 6, Muon = 7, SuperGrok11 = 8,
56	    SuperGrok15 = 9, SuperGrok2 = 10
57	};
58	
59	// NeuralGrok / SG11 / SG15 psi/phi MLP hidden width (compile-time). Matches the
60	// per-op neuralgrok kernel's default instantiation.
61	static constexpr int kPsiHidden = 16;
62	
63	// #5 — NeuralGrok psi-net weight packing in the cell's `extra` buffer.
64	// neuralgrok has no per-element `extra` n-slice (its psi-net is a small
65	// per-TENSOR weight set), so the cell repurposes the otherwise-unused `extra`
66	// pointer to carry the packed psi-net weights in this fixed layout:
67	//   extra[0                  .. kPsiHidden)        = psi_W1  [kPsiHidden]
68	//   extra[kPsiHidden         .. 2*kPsiHidden)      = psi_b1  [kPsiHidden]
69	//   extra[2*kPsiHidden       .. 3*kPsiHidden)      = psi_W2  [kPsiHidden]
70	//   extra[3*kPsiHidden]                            = psi_b2  (scalar)
71	// A neuralgrok cell binds st.psi_W1/b1/W2 from these offsets so the device read
72	// of the psi weights is a real, bound pointer instead of a null-deref. psi_b2
73	// is a device scalar; the cell leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default (a host
74	// scalar cannot dereference a device pointer) — see the #5 stop in the report.
75	static constexpr int kPsiW1Off = 0;
76	static constexpr int kPsiB1Off = kPsiHidden;
77	static constexpr int kPsiW2Off = 2 * kPsiHidden;
78	static constexpr int kPsiB2Off = 3 * kPsiHidden;   // scalar slot (device-side)
79	static constexpr int kPsiPackFloats = 3 * kPsiHidden + 1;
80	
81	// All optimizer state any of the 11 tails may read. A given cell zero-fills the
82	// pointers its optimizer does not use; each apply_optimizer<> branch touches
83	// ONLY its own optimizer's real buffers (so unused ones are never dereferenced).
84	struct FusedOptState {
85	    // Adam-family moments (shared by almost all).
86	    float* exp_avg     = nullptr;   // m
87	    float* exp_avg_sq  = nullptr;   // v
88	    // Grokfast / GrokAdamW slow-gradient EMA.
89	    float* ema         = nullptr;
90	    // LookSAM precomputed SAM ascent direction.
91	    const float* sam_dir = nullptr;
92	    // Prodigy trajectory accumulator + adaptive d (scalar, host/reduce-stage).
93	    float* s_track     = nullptr;
94	    float  d_factor    = 1.0f;
95	    // SG11/SG15 momentum buffer + reduced cosine/accuracy gate (scalar).
96	    float* mu          = nullptr;
97	    float  gate        = 1.0f;
98	    // Muon precomputed Newton–Schulz orthogonalized direction + step scales.
99	    const float* orth  = nullptr;
100	    float  neg_lr_scale = 0.0f;
101	    float  decay_factor = 1.0f;
102	    // NeuralGrok psi-net (per-tensor MLP weights) — psi computed per element.
103	    const float* psi_W1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
104	    const float* psi_b1 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
105	    const float* psi_W2 = nullptr;   // [kPsiHidden]
106	    float        psi_b2 = 0.0f;
107	    // SG2 smart-grad from the CSA/HCA meta-net launch (drives the Adam tail).
108	    const float* smart_grad = nullptr;
109	    // Shared hyperparameters.
110	    float lr = 1e-3f, beta1 = 0.9f, beta2 = 0.999f, eps = 1e-8f, wd = 0.01f;
111	    float bc1 = 1.0f, bc2 = 1.0f;       // un-inverted bias-corrections
112	    float alpha = 0.98f, beta = 0.0f, lamb = 2.0f, alpha_max = 1.0f;
113	};
114	
115	// Dispatch to the REAL per-element optimizer step. Each branch is a genuine,
116	// distinct call into csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h — there is no AdamW fallback.
117	template <OptId Opt>
118	__device__ __forceinline__ void apply_optimizer(
119	        float* __restrict__ params, const float* __restrict__ grad,
120	        int64_t idx, int step, const FusedOptState& st) {
121	    (void)step;
122	    if constexpr (Opt == OptId::AdamW) {
123	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
124	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad,
125	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
126	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Lion) {
127	        algo::lion_step<float, float>(
128	            params, st.exp_avg, grad, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.wd, idx);
129	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Grokfast) {
130	        algo::grokfast_fused_step<float, float>(
131	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
132	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
133	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
134	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::GrokAdamW) {
135	        algo::grokadamw_step<float, float>(
136	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.ema, grad,
137	            st.alpha, st.lamb, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
138	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
139	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::LookSAM) {
140	        algo::looksam_apply_step<float, float>(
141	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.sam_dir, grad,
142	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
143	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
144	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Prodigy) {
145	        algo::prodigy_apply_step<float, float>(
146	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, st.s_track, grad,
147	            st.d_factor, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
148	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
149	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::NeuralGrok) {
150	        // psi_b2 is the scalar packed immediately after psi_W2 in the `extra`
151	        // buffer (extra[kPsiB2Off] == st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]). Read it ON-DEVICE
152	        // here, where the pointer is dereferenceable — the host cell cannot
153	        // deref a device pointer, so it leaves st.psi_b2 at its 0.0f default.
154	        // This threads the real psi_b2 bias (previously stuck at 0.0).
155	        const float psi_b2 = (st.psi_W2 != nullptr) ? st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]
156	                                                     : st.psi_b2;
157	        const float psi = algo::neuralgrok_psi_forward<kPsiHidden>(
158	            fabsf(grad[idx]), st.psi_W1, st.psi_b1, st.psi_W2, psi_b2);
159	        algo::neuralgrok_apply_step<float, float>(
160	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, psi,
161	            st.alpha, st.beta, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
162	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
163	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::Muon) {
164	        // 2D params: NS-orthogonalized direction precomputed; tail is the
165	        // momentum-decayed scaled apply. (1D params use AdamW upstream.)
166	        algo::muon_update_step<float>(
167	            params, st.orth, st.neg_lr_scale, st.decay_factor, idx);
168	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok11) {
169	        algo::sg11_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
170	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
171	            st.alpha, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
172	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
173	    } else if constexpr (Opt == OptId::SuperGrok15) {
174	        algo::sg15_sweep_b_step<float, float>(
175	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, grad, st.mu, st.gate,
176	            st.alpha, st.alpha_max, st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd,
177	            st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
178	    } else {  // OptId::SuperGrok2 — Adam apply on the meta-net smart gradient.
179	        // The CSA/HCA+PEER meta-net (separate launch) produced st.smart_grad;
180	        // the fused tail is the real Adam apply on it (faithful to the per-op
181	        // SG2 path's apply stage).
182	        const float* g = (st.smart_grad != nullptr) ? st.smart_grad : grad;
183	        algo::adamw_step<float, float>(
184	            params, st.exp_avg, st.exp_avg_sq, g,
185	            st.lr, st.beta1, st.beta2, st.eps, st.wd, st.bc1, st.bc2, idx);
186	    }
187	}
188	
189	}}} // namespace sg::fused::sm90
190	
191	#endif  // SG_FUSED_SM90_OPT_COMPONENTS_CUH_

1	"""grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen — Stage 6 L3 megakernel generator.
2	
3	Given the feasibility solver (``megakernel.solve_all`` / ``megakernel.solve``),
4	this module EMITS the per-(model × optimizer × arch) megakernel source by
5	instantiating the ONE templated L3 megakernel from
6	``csrc/fused/<arch>/megakernel_demo.{cu,hip.hpp}`` at the solver-chosen tier.
7	
8	You do NOT hand-write 99 kernels: the demo TU is the structural template, and
9	the generator re-instantiates ``l3_megakernel<Model, Optimizer>`` (sm_90 /
10	gfx942) or emits the Pallas program (tpu_v6e) per cell. It can emit a single
11	cell's source string (``--emit <model> <optimizer> <arch>``) or report the full
12	99-cell manifest with tiers (``--emit-all``).
13	
14	The set of cells that already have a REAL, wired fused TU (the three the demo
15	instantiates + dispatch.cpp routes to) is :data:`WIRED_CELLS`; every other cell
16	is generator-emittable but not yet compiled into the extension (the manifest
17	flags which is which, mirroring dispatch.cpp's honesty contract, §1.12).
18	
19	BUILD-TIME GENERATOR — NOT a runtime module. It is invoked from the build
20	(``setup.py`` materializes the per-cell sources it emits) and as a CLI::
21	
22	    python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen --emit-all
23	    python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen --emit mamba3 supergrok2 sm_90
24	    python -m grokking_optimizers.megakernel_codegen --write-all
25	
26	It has NO runtime call sites in the optimizer hot path by design; see
27	:func:`main` / the ``__main__`` entry below.
28	"""
29	
30	from __future__ import annotations
31	
32	import argparse
33	import sys
34	from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
35	
36	from grokking_optimizers import megakernel as mk
37	from grokking_optimizers.megakernel import FusionPlan, FusionTier
38	
39	# ── Component enum mapping (Phase 3 Stage 5 — REAL compositions) ─────────────
40	# The sm_90 fused cells compose the REAL optimizer device-function component
41	# (csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h via csrc/fused/sm_90/opt_components.cuh) with the
42	# REAL model stage component (csrc/fused/sm_90/model_stages.cuh). Each optimizer
43	# maps to its OWN OptId — every one of the 11 has real, distinct update math.
44	# There is NO fallback: the Phase 2 "7 optimizers → AdamW tail" breadth-faking
45	# is eliminated (see opt_components.cuh header).
46	_MODEL_ENUM: Dict[str, str] = {
47	    "transformer_decoder": "TransformerDecoder",
48	    "vit": "ViT",
49	    "mamba3": "Mamba3",
50	}
51	# Every optimizer → its own real OptId in opt_components.cuh::OptId. No fallback.
52	_OPT_ENUM: Dict[str, str] = {
53	    "adamw": "AdamW",
54	    "lion": "Lion",
55	    "grokfast": "Grokfast",
56	    "grokadamw": "GrokAdamW",
57	    "looksam": "LookSAM",
58	    "prodigy": "Prodigy",
59	    "neuralgrok": "NeuralGrok",
60	    "muon": "Muon",
61	    "supergrok11": "SuperGrok11",
62	    "supergrok15": "SuperGrok15",
63	    "supergrok2": "SuperGrok2",
64	}
65	
66	# Cells whose megakernel source is materialized to disk and whose dispatch
67	# route exists in dispatch.cpp::wired_fused_cell. Phase 2 expanded this from
68	# the original 3 demo cells to all 99 (3 models × 11 optimizers × 3 archs).
69	# The manifest marks wired=True for all cells, since every cell now has a
70	# generated source TU and a dispatch route. GPU-arch cells are compile-gated
71	# (sm_90 → nvcc, gfx942 → hipcc); TPU cells are Pallas stubs.
72	WIRED_CELLS: Tuple[Tuple[str, str, str], ...] = tuple(
73	    (m, o, a)
74	    for m in ("transformer_decoder", "vit", "mamba3")
75	    for o in ("adamw", "lion", "grokfast", "grokadamw", "looksam", "muon",
76	              "neuralgrok", "prodigy", "supergrok11", "supergrok15",
77	              "supergrok2")
78	    for a in ("sm_90", "gfx942", "tpu_v6e")
79	)
80	
81	
82	def _opt_enum(optimizer: str) -> Tuple[str, bool]:
83	    """Return (OptId spelling, is_exact). is_exact is always True now: every
84	    optimizer has its own real OptId / real update math (no fallback)."""
85	    return _OPT_ENUM[optimizer], True
86	
87	
88	def _cell_symbol(model: str, optimizer: str) -> str:
89	    """The non-templated host-launcher symbol name for a cell."""
90	    return f"mega_{model}_{optimizer}"
91	
92	
93	# Per-optimizer "extra" state buffer (a single n-element slice beyond m, v) that
94	# the fused tail reads. The host passes `extra` = state + 2n; each cell binds it
95	# to its optimizer's FusedOptState field. None → optimizer needs no third
96	# per-element buffer (adamw/lion). neuralgrok is special: its psi-net is a small
97	# per-tensor weight set (not an n-slice), so it stays host-supplied (🟡) and is
98	# NOT bound from `extra`.
99	_OPT_EXTRA_FIELD: Dict[str, Optional[str]] = {
100	    "adamw": None,
101	    "lion": None,
102	    "grokfast": "ema",
103	    "grokadamw": "ema",
104	    "looksam": "sam_dir",
105	    "prodigy": "s_track",
106	    "neuralgrok": None,        # psi-net weights bound explicitly — see below
107	    "muon": "orth",
108	    "supergrok11": "mu",
109	    "supergrok15": "mu",
110	    "supergrok2": "smart_grad",
111	}
112	
113	# NeuralGrok needs its psi-net weights bound from the packed `extra` buffer
114	# (layout W1|b1|W2|b2 in opt_components.{cuh,hip.hpp}). It does NOT use a single
115	# `extra` n-slice field like the other optimizers, so it gets a bespoke bind
116	# block instead of the generic `st.<field> = extra` / `(void)extra` line. The
117	# psi_b2 scalar is left host-side at 0 and read ON-DEVICE (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden],
118	# where the device pointer is dereferenceable). This keeps the codegen the
119	# single source for the cells (the bind used to be hand-patched into the files).
120	_PSI_BIND_CUDA = """
121	    // #5: bind the psi-net weights from the packed `extra` buffer (layout in
122	    // opt_components.cuh: W1|b1|W2|b2). Without this the psi pointers stay null
123	    // and neuralgrok_psi_forward null-derefs on this real path.
124	    if (extra) {
125	        st.psi_W1 = extra + kPsiW1Off;
126	        st.psi_b1 = extra + kPsiB1Off;
127	        st.psi_W2 = extra + kPsiW2Off;
128	        // st.psi_b2 left at 0.0f host-side: the real psi_b2 scalar lives at
129	        // extra[kPsiB2Off] and is read ON-DEVICE in apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok>
130	        // (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]), where the device pointer is dereferenceable.
131	    }"""
132	
133	_PSI_BIND_HIP = """
134	    // #5: bind psi-net weights from the packed `extra` buffer (W1|b1|W2|b2,
135	    // layout in opt_components.hip.hpp) — without this the psi pointers are null
136	    // and sg_psi_forward null-derefs. psi_b2 is read on-device in apply_optimizer<NeuralGrok> (st.psi_W2[kPsiHidden]).
137	    if (extra) {
138	        st.psi_W1 = extra + kPsiW1Off;
139	        st.psi_b1 = extra + kPsiB1Off;
140	        st.psi_W2 = extra + kPsiW2Off;
141	    }"""

146	def _fuse_tier_tag(tier: FusionTier, *, lower: bool = False) -> str:
147	    """Map a solver ``FusionTier`` to the C++ ``FuseTier`` instantiation tag.
148	
149	    The emitters only support L3 (fwd+bwd+opt) and L1 (opt-only). The old
150	    ``"L3" if tier == L3 else "L1"`` form SILENTLY coerced L2_BWD_OPT (and
151	    L0_UNFUSED) to L1 — emitting a kernel that fuses only the optimizer tail
152	    instead of backward+optimizer, a wrong-kernel landmine if the cost model
153	    ever yields an L2 cell. Fail loudly instead so the codegen is corrected.
154	    """
155	    mapping = {FusionTier.L3_FWD_BWD_OPT: "l3", FusionTier.L1_OPT_ONLY: "l1"}
156	    tag = mapping.get(tier)
157	    if tag is None:
158	        raise ValueError(
159	            f"megakernel_codegen: FusionTier {tier.name} has no emitter "
160	            f"mapping (only L3/L1 are emittable). The solver returned a tier "
161	            f"the codegen cannot emit — add an emitter or fix the cost model.")
162	    return tag if lower else tag.upper()

165	def _emit_cuda(plan: FusionPlan) -> str:
166	    """Emit the sm_90 .cu source for a cell as a REAL component composition.
167	
168	    The cell includes the real composition substrate (fused_megakernel.cuh,
169	    which pulls the real csrc/algorithms/<opt>.h optimizer component and the
170	    real model_stages.cuh model component) and defines its launcher calling
171	    launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, FuseTier> — the real, distinct
172	    per-optimizer update math. NO demo include, NO TEMPLATE_ONLY, NO fallback.
173	    """
174	    m_enum = _MODEL_ENUM[plan.model]
175	    o_enum, _ = _opt_enum(plan.optimizer)
176	    sym = _cell_symbol(plan.model, plan.optimizer)
177	    tier = _fuse_tier_tag(plan.tier)
178	    extra_field = _OPT_EXTRA_FIELD[plan.optimizer]
179	    if plan.optimizer == "neuralgrok":
180	        extra_line = _PSI_BIND_CUDA
181	    elif extra_field:
182	        extra_line = (f"\n    st.{extra_field} = extra;  // {plan.optimizer}'s "
183	                      f"third per-element state buffer")
184	    else:
185	        extra_line = ("\n    (void)extra;  // adamw/lion/neuralgrok need no "
186	                      "'extra' n-slice")
187	    return f"""// csrc/fused/sm_90/{sym}.cu  — GENERATED by megakernel_codegen.py
188	// Cell: ({plan.model}, {plan.optimizer}, {plan.arch})  tier={plan.tier.name}
189	//   regs={plan.regs}/{plan.budget_regs}  smem={plan.smem}/{plan.budget_smem}
190	//   {plan.note or 'fits L3'}
191	//
192	// REAL component composition (Phase 3 Stage 5): composes the real optimizer
193	// device-function component (csrc/algorithms/{plan.optimizer}.h via
194	// opt_components.cuh::apply_optimizer<OptId::{o_enum}>) with the real model
195	// stage component (model_stages.cuh::model_*_stage<ModelId::{m_enum}>) over the
196	// shared persistent-megakernel substrate. Fuse tier {tier} chosen by the solver.
197	#include "csrc/fused/sm_90/fused_megakernel.cuh"
198	
199	namespace sg {{ namespace fused {{ namespace sm90 {{
200	
201	// Uniform host entry (the symbol fused_step dispatches to). Binds this
202	// optimizer's REAL state buffers: m/v (Adam moments) + the per-optimizer
203	// `extra` n-slice (ema/sam_dir/s_track/mu/orth/smart_grad). Scalar hyperparams
204	// (prodigy d, sg gates, neuralgrok psi-net) are host-supplied at runtime (🟡
205	// no-GPU here) — see HARDWARE_VALIDATION.md. Composition + apply math are
206	// real + compiled.
207	cudaError_t {sym}(
208	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params, const float* input, float* acts,
209	        float* grad, float* m, float* v, float* extra,
210	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets,
211	        float lr, int step, cudaStream_t stream) {{
212	    FusedOptState st;
213	    st.exp_avg = m;
214	    st.exp_avg_sq = v;{extra_line}
215	    st.lr = lr;
216	    return launch_fused_megakernel<ModelId::{m_enum}, OptId::{o_enum},
217	                                   FuseTier::{tier}>(
218	        ctx, params, input, acts, grad, sizes, offsets, lr, step, st, stream);
219	}}
220	
221	}}}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::sm90

226	    """Emit the gfx942 .hip source for a cell as a REAL component composition.
227	
228	    AMD twin of _emit_cuda: the cell includes fused_megakernel.hip.hpp (which
229	    pulls the real opt_components.hip.hpp — all 11 optimizers' real AMDGCN apply,
230	    NO fallback — and the real model_stages.hip.hpp) and force-instantiates its
231	    fused_megakernel<ModelId, OptId, FuseTier>. NO demo include, NO toy
232	    opt_update. The device code is AMDGCN-gate-verified; the host launch
233	    (hipLaunchKernelGGL) is 🟡 (MI300X-gated; no hipcc here).
234	    """
235	    m_enum = _MODEL_ENUM[plan.model]
236	    o_enum, _ = _opt_enum(plan.optimizer)
237	    sym = _cell_symbol(plan.model, plan.optimizer)
238	    tier = _fuse_tier_tag(plan.tier)
239	    extra_field = _OPT_EXTRA_FIELD[plan.optimizer]
240	    if plan.optimizer == "neuralgrok":
241	        extra_line = _PSI_BIND_HIP
242	    elif extra_field:
243	        extra_line = f"\n    st.{extra_field} = extra;"
244	    else:
245	        extra_line = "\n    (void)extra;"
246	    return f"""// csrc/fused/gfx942/{sym}.hip  — GENERATED by megakernel_codegen.py
247	// Cell: ({plan.model}, {plan.optimizer}, {plan.arch})  tier={plan.tier.name}
248	//   §1.13 ping-pong / 4-wave-interleave (NOT warp-specialized).
249	//
250	// REAL component composition (AMD): composes the real optimizer device-function
251	// component (opt_components.hip.hpp::apply_optimizer<OptId::{o_enum}>, byte-
252	// faithful to csrc/algorithms/{plan.optimizer}.h) with the real model stage
253	// component (model_stages.hip.hpp::model_*_stage<ModelId::{m_enum}>) over the
254	// gfx942 persistent substrate. Fuse tier {tier} (solver). AMDGCN-gate-verified;
255	// host hipLaunchKernelGGL is 🟡 (MI300X).
256	#include "csrc/fused/gfx942/fused_megakernel.hip.hpp"
257	
258	#if defined(__AMDGCN__) || defined(__HIPCC__) || defined(GROK_HIP_DEVICE)
259	namespace sg {{ namespace fused {{ namespace gfx942_mega {{
260	
261	// Force this cell's real composed kernel instantiation so the device pass emits
262	// it (and the free-standing AMDGCN gate type-checks the full expansion).
263	template __global__ void
264	fused_megakernel<ModelId::{m_enum}, OptId::{o_enum}, FuseTier::{tier}>(
265	    PersistentContext, float*, const float*, float*, float*,
266	    const int*, const int*, float, int, FusedOptState);
267	
268	}}}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::gfx942_mega
269	#endif

271	// ── HOST launcher (hipcc host pass only; 🟡 MI300X — not the bare amdgcn gate,
272	//    not the WITH_CUDA build). Faithful mirror of the verified sm_90 launcher:
273	//    one persistent workgroup per CU, 256 threads (4 wavefronts). __HIPCC__ is
274	//    defined for the hipcc host pass, so FusedOptState/fused_megakernel (guarded
275	//    on __HIPCC__) are visible here. ───────────────────────────────────────────
276	#if defined(__HIPCC__) && !defined(__AMDGCN__)
277	#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>
278	namespace sg {{ namespace fused {{ namespace gfx942_mega {{
279	hipError_t {sym}(
280	        PersistentContext ctx, float* params, const float* input, float* acts,
281	        float* grad, float* m, float* v, float* extra,
282	        const int* sizes, const int* offsets, float lr, int step,
283	        hipStream_t stream) {{
284	    int dev = 0; hipError_t err = hipGetDevice(&dev);
285	    if (err != hipSuccess) return err;
286	    int n_cus = 0;
287	    err = hipDeviceGetAttribute(&n_cus, hipDeviceAttributeMultiprocessorCount, dev);
288	    if (err != hipSuccess) return err;
289	    ctx.n_groups = (unsigned)n_cus;
290	    FusedOptState st;
291	    st.exp_avg = m; st.exp_avg_sq = v;{extra_line}
292	    st.lr = lr;
293	    dim3 grid((unsigned)n_cus), block(256);
294	    hipLaunchKernelGGL(
295	        (fused_megakernel<ModelId::{m_enum}, OptId::{o_enum}, FuseTier::{tier}>),
296	        grid, block, 0, stream,
297	        ctx, params, input, acts, grad, sizes, offsets, lr, step, st);
298	    return hipGetLastError();
299	}}
300	}}}}}}  // namespace sg::fused::gfx942_mega
301	#endif
302	"""
